title: An analysis of stigma and suicide literacy in responses to suicides broadcast on social media
screen_reason: Alongside a classifier-building component (which on its own would be excluded as detection work), the paper reports a human content analysis of 4,969 Weibo posts responding to broadcast suicides, of which 11.67% (n=580) 'contained misinformation about suicide' — incorrect knowledge of the signs or treatments of suicide coded against a published suicide-literacy framework. That is a CONTENT share with an explicit denominator.

estimates.date: Posts downloaded March 2015 (posts of 1.06 million active users)
estimates.measure_type: % of Weibo posts responding to suicides broadcast on social media that contained misinformation about suicide (incorrect knowledge of suicide signs or treatments)
estimates.denominator: 4,969 Weibo posts related to social media suicide, retained from 6,632 keyword-matched posts after excluding non-suicidal uses of the keywords (e.g. TV programmes), posts reflecting the poster's own attempt rather than a response, posts about attempters whose suicidal posts were released after death, posts not in Chinese or English, and posts uncodable for lack of context
estimates.definition: Post coded into one of eight categories of incorrect knowledge about the signs or treatments of suicide — e.g. 'suicide happens without warning', 'people who want to attempt suicide cannot change their mind quickly', 'people who have thoughts about suicide should not tell others about it', 'nothing can be done to stop people once they have made up their minds'; posts fitting no category were coded 'irrelevant'
estimates.misinfo_def: “The coding framework was based on previous research investigating suicide literacy, which has described categories of incorrect knowledge regarding the signs and treatments of suicide”
estimates.source_quote: 11.67% of the Weibo posts (n = 580) contained misinformation about suicide.
estimates.page_loc: Abstract (Results); Results §3.2 and Table 1 (n = 580); Discussion p. 7 ('A total of 11.67% of posts conveyed incorrect knowledge regarding signs and treatments of suicide')
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Coding framework based on the suicide-literacy literature (Batterham et al. 2013; Calear, Batterham & Christensen 2012): one researcher classified posts inductively into an initial framework, two additional researchers gave feedback after a training session, and one extra item was added to make a set of eight. Two researchers then coded independently; Cohen's κ = 0.72 ('acceptable level of agreement'); discrepancies resolved by a third researcher's decision. (The separate stigma coding of 1,760 posts had κ = 0.73.)
estimates.moderator_quote: Secondly, in March 2015, the Weibo posts from the 1.06 million active users were downloaded, also using the application programming interface. To identify posts that were related to online suicide attempts, the collected posts were searched automatically using a set of specific keywords ... A total of 6632 posts matched these keywords. No further filtering of the raw data occurred. ... Therefore, the final sample consisted of 4969 posts.
estimates.notes: Denominator confirmed arithmetically: 580/4,969 = 11.67% (580/6,632 would be 8.75%), so the 11.67% is on the post-exclusion sample, not the raw keyword corpus. Construct is CONTENT and not a belief measure: the unit is the POST and the denominator is posts, so this is a share of items carrying incorrect claims, not a share of people holding a false belief. breadth=false because the eight categories are demonstrably incorrect factual claims about suicide signs and treatments, judged against an established literacy instrument. The classifier component of this paper (stigma detection models, F1 66.15%–72.79%) is detection work and contributes nothing extractable.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) All the category percentages in the Abstract and Discussion are shares of the 580 misinformation posts, NOT of the 4,969 corpus — easy to misread as prevalence. From Table 1: 'suicide happens without warning' 162/580 = 27.93%, 'people who want to attempt suicide cannot change their mind quickly' 105/580 = 18.10%, 'people who have thoughts about suicide should not tell others about it' 204/580 = 35.17%, signs categories overall 324/580 = 55.86%, treatments 256/580 = 44.14%. Not extracted (within-misinformation type breakdown). (2) '488 of 580 posts (84.14%) were related to different types of stigmatizing attitudes' and '214 of 488 stigmatizing posts (43.85%)' / '36.90% of posts with poor literacy also conveyed false representation stigma' — stigma, not falsity, computed inside the misinformation set. (3) The stigma arm reports '1760 posts were found to reflect stigmatizing attitudes' out of 6,632 keyword-matched posts, and '388 posts (22.05%)' of those indicating 'false representation stigma' (the belief that a broadcast attempt is not genuine, which the Introduction calls 'the misleading belief'). Not extracted: the paper frames these as stigma rather than misinformation prevalence, and their denominator is the unfiltered 6,632 corpus that the authors themselves later judged to contain irrelevant posts. An adjudicator could argue 1,760/6,632 = 26.5% is a misinformation-adjacent share, but neither that percentage nor a false-representation prevalence over the full corpus is stated verbatim, so R8 bars computing it. (4) Classification model performance (F1 72.79% and 66.15%, with precision/recall) is detection-method accuracy, not prevalence. (5) '17.96% (n = 30)' of reported Chinese suicide incidents occurring on Sina Weibo is background epidemiology cited in the Introduction, not a misinformation measure.

rob.design: Two-part observational study on Sina Weibo. Frame: a Weibo User Pool of 99,925,821 users, of which 1,953,485 were active and 1.06 million had posts exportable via the API; their posts were downloaded in March 2015 and keyword-searched for 'live broadcast of suicide', 'self-presentation of suicide' and 'suicide show' in Chinese, pinyin and English variants, returning 6,632 posts with no further filtering. For the literacy content analysis five exclusion rules reduced this to 4,969 posts. No response rate applies (public platform data; informed consent not obtained, IRB-approved as public data). Coding: framework adapted from the Literacy of Suicide Scale with one added item; two independent coders, Cohen's κ = 0.72, third-researcher adjudication of discrepancies. Authors' stated limitations: Weibo users skew young (63% of Chinese users aged 10–29) and are unrepresentative of Chinese people; Weibo only, though broadcasts occur elsewhere; unknown whether findings transfer to non-broadcast suicide.
rob.item6_quote: The coding framework was based on previous research investigating suicide literacy, which has described categories of incorrect knowledge regarding the signs and treatments of suicide (Batterham et al., 2013; Calear, Batterham, & Christensen, 2012).
rob.item10_quote: A total of 580 posts were coded as indicating a level of poor suicide literacy. Among these, 324 posts (55.86%) were related to the incorrect knowledge about suicide signs, while 256 posts (44.14%) were related to the incorrect knowledge about suicide treatments.
